description: We are the Kurupira Team, a group of researchers, students, and science and technology enthusiasts driven by curiosity and innovation. Our multidisciplinary team combines expertise in physics, software development, data analysis, electronics, engineering, and management. For the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge, we aim to develop innovative solutions for environmental monitoring and a better understanding of our planet.
summary: Kurupira, named after the forest-protecting entity from the Indigenous cultures of Brazil, is a geospatial web platform designed to support decision-making by integrating harmonized wildfire hotspot data from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS sensors across Brazilian territory. The platform combines a historical calendar, interactive map, climate context, and seasonal forecasts, allowing users to explore spatial and temporal patterns, compare historical periods, and identify anomalies. It also provides additional analyses for the Brazilian states with the largest areas of Amazon rainforest. Furthermore, it incorporates a machine learning model to estimate the distribution and intensity of fire hotspots over the coming months, identifying potentially critical areas. Kurupira aims to support preventive actions, resource allocation, and environmental monitoring, benefiting firefighters, environmental agencies, researchers, and communities vulnerable to wildfires.
details:
The Kurupira web platform is a geospatial tool for monitoring and conducting historical analyses of fire hotspots, developed to facilitate the identification of occurrence patterns and support wildfire prevention and control efforts in Brazil. Its interface features an interactive calendar synchronized with a geographic map, allowing users to visualize the distribution of fire hotspots over the years, explore different regions, select specific periods, and identify concentrations and seasonal variations. The platform also provides climate information and analytical resources to support data interpretation.

Since the MODIS and VIIRS sensors have different spatial resolutions and detection sensitivities, we developed a statistical calibration method to adjust VIIRS hotspot counts to the MODIS reference scale. To achieve this, we calculated month- and region-specific correction factors, combining regional and national information to reduce statistical fluctuations and improve data consistency. The calibration was performed using records from 2012 to 2022 and independently evaluated over the 2023–2025 period. We then applied the correction factors to daily records while preserving their original dates and geographic coordinates. Additionally, we developed an experimental approach to harmonize Fire Radiative Power (FRP) by matching MODIS and VIIRS detections occurring close to each other in both space and time, in order to establish statistical relationships between their measurements. This allowed us to incorporate adjusted FRP estimates into the integrated dataset, alongside the observed and corrected hotspot counts. The result is a harmonized historical dataset that enables more consistent analyses of spatial patterns, seasonality, and the temporal evolution of fire activity in Brazil, serving as input for climatological studies and machine learning models.

Using this same dataset, we developed a machine learning model capable of estimating which regions are most likely to experience higher concentrations of fire hotspots over the following two months. The goal is to identify potentially critical areas in advance, providing information that can assist firefighting teams, environmental agencies, and authorities in operational planning, resource allocation, and the prioritization of monitoring activities.

In addition to nationwide monitoring, Kurupira provides complementary analyses for the Brazilian states of Amazonas, Pará, and Mato Grosso, which together encompass approximately 77% of the Amazon rainforest within Brazilian territory. To deepen the regional analysis, we cross-referenced fire hotspot data from these areas with scientific studies, including Kumar et al. (2014), Santos, Silva, and Guimarães (2020), and Mota et al. (2019). This approach seeks to relate the observed patterns to environmental and territorial aspects discussed in the scientific literature, providing a broader understanding of the distribution of fire hotspots and the factors associated with fire occurrence in the Amazon region.

As an additional feature, the platform allows users to export the available data and analysis results in both CSV and PDF formats, facilitating data storage, further analysis, and the generation of reports for research and decision-making purposes.

Technologies and Resources Used:

  • Frontend: React with TypeScript, built with Vite and styled with Emotion (CSS-in-JS). The interactive map is rendered with MapLibre GL from vector GeoJSON layers. Claude Code was used as an AI-assisted development tool to accelerate implementation and improve the development workflow.
  • Backend: Python. A FastAPI service queries Parquet files with DuckDB and serves JSON, GeoJSON and CSV. A data pipeline (pandas, PyArrow, Shapely) processes and aggregates the MODIS/VIIRS hotspot data, and a Google Earth Engine script adds deforestation data. Both are deployed on Vercel. Claude Code was also used to accelerate code development, debugging, and implementation.
  • Repository and Version Control: GitHub, used to store, organize, and version the project's source code.
  • Hosting and Deployment: Vercel, used to host both the web app and the Python API (as serverless functions), with automatic deployments from the GitHub repository.
  • Domain: Porkbun, used to register the project's custom domain, offered free of charge through the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
  • Data Processing and Analysis: Python, used for collecting, harmonizing, organizing, and analyzing data from the MODIS and VIIRS sensors.
  • Machine Learning: Python, employed in the development, training, and evaluation of the predictive model, with ChatGPT used as an AI-assisted tool to support model development, code refinement, and analysis.
  • Pitch Production: YouTube (video publication), ElevenLabs (AI-generated voice narration), and Claude Pro (support in preparing and refining the presentation).

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/lbresteves/NASASpaceApps-kurupira
